market_brief: Asia extended Monday's Nvidia-led squeeze (S&P 500 +4.7% to 7,237, SOX +14%, VIX 26.6): the Kospi gained about 6% toward 4,970 and the Nikkei about 3.6-3.9%, snapping an eight-day losing run for MSCI Asia Pacific, but Hong Kong slipped about 0.9% after the US blacklisted an Alibaba Singapore unit, and Nasdaq and Euro Stoxx futures are about 0.2% lower. The rally sits on hawkish rates: Williams said inflation risks are skewed up, the 2-year stopped through at 4.70% at auction, the 10-year holds near 4.92-4.93% and the DXY near 104.3, while BoE's Pill also struck a hawkish tone. Commodities stay soft after Brent's 6% drop to about $86.8, with WTI off another 0.6% despite three tankers reportedly hitting Hormuz mines; gold (~$3,628) eased 0.4% and bitcoin briefly dipped under $60k. India reopens Wednesday after Monday's 1.75% Nifty drop, with Gift Nifty pointing flat; Dell, HP, Workday and Autodesk report after the US close.
ai_brief: Efficiency is the theme: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini reuses looped layers to match larger open models at a fraction of the cost, and DeepMind says agent teams with formal verification cut a quantum algorithm's estimated cost 11.8x. Security tooling and agents keep spreading, with OpenAI and Cisco's open-source Shirudo runtime and Canva's MCP going GA. Legal and policy pressure is rising, from state lawsuits over Grok images to Reuters' account of why the White House pushed Huang's return.

items.headline: Update: Kospi ends about 6% higher and Nikkei near 4% as Asia snaps an eight-day losing streak
items.summary: After the early sidecar trigger, the Kospi held a gain of roughly 6% near 4,970 while Japan rose about 3.6-3.9% and the ASX 1.5-1.8%, lifting MSCI Asia Pacific 1.5% after eight straight declines. TSMC and Hon Hai rose close to double digits in Taiwan.

items.headline: Hang Seng lags the rally after the US blacklists Alibaba's Singapore unit; Alibaba vows legal action
items.summary: Washington added Alibaba's Singapore-based Apex Enterprise Solutions and AI-infrastructure firm Megaspeed to its trade blacklist; Alibaba said it will pursue legal action and Singapore said its Megaspeed probe continues. The Hang Seng erased opening gains to trade about 0.9% lower while Shanghai was roughly flat.

items.headline: Update: Nvidia adds a national-security and export-controls board committee as Congress signals an inquiry
items.summary: Alongside reinstating Huang, Nvidia said independent directors are still reviewing the resignation episode and it will create an export-controls committee and hire a chief compliance officer. House Democratic Leader Jeffries said Congress will investigate, and the administration reportedly stressed export-control compliance.

items.headline: Williams details hawkish view: inflation seen at 3.5% at end-2026 and back to 2% only in 2028
items.summary: NY Fed President Williams said inflation is still too high with risks skewed to the upside, though he does not see pressures broadening; markets read the remarks as backing a December hike. Separately, the Fed's watchdog is reportedly reviewing Vice Chair Bowman's attendance at a Bank of America client dinner.

items.headline: BoE's Pill says action is needed now on inflation; ANZ pulls its RBA cut forecast to June 2027
items.summary: BoE chief economist Huw Pill argued for acting now to preserve price stability, adding to hawkish central-bank rhetoric. ANZ moved its first RBA rate-cut call to June 2027 from November 2027, after five RBA hikes this year.

items.headline: Two-year auction stops through at 4.700% as high-yield spreads tighten by double digits
items.summary: The $69bn 2-year sale priced at 4.700% versus 4.703% when-issued with a 2.65x bid-to-cover; 5- and 7-year auctions follow this week. US high-yield spreads tightened by double digits Monday after widening 51bp the prior week.

items.headline: Macron proposes a constitutional 'golden rule' for balanced budgets as French PMI contracts sharply
items.summary: Macron proposed enshrining a multi-year path to balanced budgets in the constitution, which would need a three-fifths parliamentary majority. France's flash PMI showed the sharpest private-sector contraction in six months.

items.headline: IRGC says three tankers caught fire after hitting Hormuz mines; Qatar works to revive US-Iran talks
items.summary: Iran's IRGC reported mine strikes on three tankers, Kpler says Iran appears to be probing the US naval blockade with spoofed signals, and Qatar's PM met Vance and Rubio to restart negotiations. WTI still slipped about 0.6% in Asia after Monday's 4.5% fall, while European gas rallied on colder forecasts.

items.headline: Gold, copper and bitcoin give back some of Monday's bounce; BTC briefly breaks below $60k
items.summary: Spot gold eased about 0.4% and LME copper fell about 2.4% in Asian trade after Monday's rebounds. Bitcoin dropped about 1.3%, briefly trading under $60,000 before recovering most of the move.

items.headline: Petrobras lifts its five-year investment plan to $122bn and targets 2.9m bpd
items.summary: Petrobras raised planned five-year capex to $122bn from $109bn and set a 2.9m barrels-per-day output target, assuming Brent at $74 for 2027.

items.headline: ConocoPhillips agrees to sell its Norwegian business to Var Energi for $3.9bn
items.summary: ConocoPhillips will divest its Norway operations to Var Energi in a $3.9bn deal, continuing portfolio pruning among US majors.

items.headline: Singapore revises Q3 GDP sharply higher to 6.1% y/y
items.summary: Final Q3 growth came in at 1.5% q/q and 6.1% y/y, above forecasts of 1.3% and 5.6% and the preliminary 1.1% and 5.4%.

items.headline: India shut for Guru Nanak Jayanti; Gift Nifty signals a flat reopening Wednesday
items.summary: Gift Nifty indicated a flat start against Monday's Nifty close of 25,349.65 after a 1.75% fall, though Asia's rally since then could change that. Per HDFC SKY, foreign investors bought a record $13bn of Indian equities in November, cutting year-to-date outflows to $18.4bn.

items.headline: Positioning: AUD risk reversals most USD-bullish since April as index futures cool
items.summary: Saxo notes one-month AUD/USD implied volatility at a six-month high and risk reversals at 156bp in favour of the dollar, signalling demand for downside protection. Nasdaq 100 futures eased about 0.2% in Asia after Monday's squeeze.

items.headline: US reportedly delays Patriot shipments as NATO authorises forward AWACS deployment
items.summary: About 60 Patriot interceptors reportedly await Pentagon approval, per the FT, and NATO approved forward AWACS deployment after airspace violations over Poland.

items.headline: Today: German Ifo, Xiaomi results and US earnings from Dell, HP, Workday, Autodesk and Best Buy
items.summary: Tuesday also brings Medtronic, Analog Devices, Dollar Tree and Abercrombie, plus speeches by ECB's Vujcic, BoC's Macklem and BoE's Greene. Wednesday has Deere, Li Auto, US PCE and GDP; US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving.

items.headline: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini loops its middle layers to cut memory and cost
items.summary: The 26.4B-parameter model repeats its middle 12 layers three times per token and fits in about 20 GB; it posted 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1. Per Artificial Analysis it matched a comparable Qwen model on its index at roughly a sixth of the per-task cost.

items.headline: DeepMind agent teams find faster quantum algorithms, verified with formal proofs
items.summary: DeepMind says multi-agent systems improved quantum algorithms for fusion-related simulation, cutting estimated compute cost about 11.8x, with results checked by a formal proof system.

items.headline: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime for stopgap exploit protection
items.summary: Shirudo applies temporary protections while patches are prepared; in a test, a Codex-generated rule reportedly blocked a Java exploit. Details are as described in roundup coverage.

items.headline: Canva's MCP server goes generally available with new REST APIs and CLI
items.summary: Agents can now create editable Canva designs and generate media through the MCP server and new developer tooling.

items.headline: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX entities over Grok-generated sexualised images
items.summary: The states allege inadequate safeguards and misleading safety claims around Grok image generation, including images involving minors, and seek penalties and injunctions.

items.headline: Trump reportedly saw Huang as key to US open-weight AI when pushing his return
items.summary: Reuters, citing sources, reports Trump and Vance intervened because they viewed Huang as a protector of America's open-weight model efforts.

items.headline: Prosecutors allege ex-OpenAI engineer used Codex to manage covert office recordings
items.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan has pleaded not guilty to an unlawful-interception charge; he is not charged with espionage or trade-secret theft.

items.headline: NHS begins recruiting for an AI breast-screening trial of nearly 700,000 women
items.summary: The three-year trial will test whether AI helps radiologists spot cancers earlier and speeds mammogram reading.

items.headline: Mystery coding model 'HungerG' appears in Qoder, free to try through Nov 30
items.summary: Qoder has not disclosed who built the model, prompting speculation on X about its origin.

items.headline: Supertake raises a $20m seed for agents that turn market views into stock portfolios
items.summary: The startup's agents convert users' predictions into portfolios; the product is in waitlisted beta.

items.headline: OpenAI's OpenWorks pays local partners up to $8,000 a month to bring AI to small businesses
items.summary: Participating firms get free consulting and three months of ChatGPT Business, per Decrypt.

items.headline: AWS survey: most APAC firms say AI returns beat costs, but few can measure ROI confidently
items.summary: 58% of AI-using businesses said gains exceeded initial costs, yet only 12% were very confident in measuring returns.
